# Know what the deployable image guarantees

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `devops-container-delivery` · **DevOps, Containers & Delivery** · Catalog level: foundation

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S05-Q035](#S05-Q035)

<p>What application-delivery problem does Docker address, and which deployment problems remain outside that boundary?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Deliver an identifiable application image while explaining its host, configuration and secret boundaries.</p>

<ul>
<li>Explain what packaging reproduces and which environment differences remain.</li>
<li>Choose container or virtual-machine isolation for the workload.</li>
<li>Trace layers and build stages into final-image contents.</li>
<li>Explain configuration and secret delivery without claiming protection from a location name alone.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

No catalog prerequisite. Establish the terms and scenario assumptions in the foundation questions before progressing; a published lesson is not evidence that you know them.

<p>Docker addresses part of the journey from source code to a running process. Compare the host boundary, then trace the build into an image and the image into a configured application. That sequence separates what is fixed in the artifact from what deployment must provide.</p>

<a id="S05-Q035"></a>

### S05-Q035 · Foundation

<p>What application-delivery problem does Docker address, and which deployment problems remain outside that boundary?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q035](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q035)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q035](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q035)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What problem does Docker solve in application delivery?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Use the journey from a developer’s environment to a running deployment. Explain what is packaged and reproduced rather than describing Docker only as a command-line tool.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Describe a packaging and runtime boundary with a concrete operational limit.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use an ASP.NET Core application as context; distinguish its image from host, network, data and external services.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connects a reproducibility problem to what a container image captures.</li>
<li>Identifies a deployment difference still requiring configuration or verification.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Claiming that a working local container guarantees the application will behave correctly in production.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would you inspect if the same image works locally but fails after deployment?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q036"></a>

### S05-Q036 · Foundation

<p>How would you compare containers and virtual machines when choosing a deployment boundary?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q036](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q036)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q036](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q036)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Compare containers and virtual machines.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Discuss what each unit contains, where isolation is provided and what the workload requires. Avoid choosing from a simple “lighter versus heavier” slogan.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose an isolation model from workload and operating constraints.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Clarify host platform, trust level, resource needs and management requirements; platform-specific guarantees need separate verification.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explains the relevant boundaries using one application and its host.</li>
<li>States an isolation or compatibility requirement that would change the choice.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Comparing only startup speed without explaining isolation, host dependency or evidence.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would you verify before running workloads with different trust levels on the same host?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S05-Q037 · Mechanism

<p>How do image layers and multi-stage builds shape the build process and the final application image?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q037](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q037)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q037](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q037)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain image layers and multi-stage builds.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Trace a source change through build stages to the deployable artifact. Explain the purpose of each stage and what should be inspected in the result.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reason about build inputs, intermediate artifacts and final-image contents.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a Docker build for a .NET application; identify builder, base-image and SDK/runtime versions. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explains layer or stage responsibilities with a concrete build change.</li>
<li>Verifies final-image contents and identifies a change that affects rebuild behavior.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Repeating “smaller image” without showing which files or build dependencies the final artifact contains.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you check whether a credential used during the build appears in the image?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q039"></a>

### S05-Q039 · Application

<p>Which configuration would you supply through environment variables, and which would you manage through a secret store?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q039](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q039)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q039](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q039)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What belongs in environment variables versus a secret store?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Compare access, exposure and update needs for ordinary settings and secret material. The delivery mechanism and the location that owns a secret need separate consideration.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose configuration delivery while accounting for credential exposure and lifecycle.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name the hosting platform and secret provider; consider process access, logging, rotation and how the application obtains values. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explains who can access each value and how it reaches the process.</li>
<li>Proposes a rotation or exposure test that checks the claimed protection.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming an environment variable is automatically a secure secret store.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you change a database credential without putting it into a build artifact?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>A .NET container works locally but fails in staging after a database credential changes. Inspect the image identity and contents, deployment settings and credential access. Explain how you would reproduce the failure without exposing secrets, identify the responsible boundary and verify the proposed correction. Use the related environment-configuration question when comparing promotion across environments.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Explains images, containers, virtual machines and build stages with a clear packaging example.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Traces artifact contents and host/runtime inputs, defends isolation and secret handling, and chooses evidence that distinguishes a build error from a deployment error.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>A successful local run or a small image size alone does not show isolation suitability, credential protection or production compatibility.</p>
